open_points.subject: A03 fresh-import trapping
open_points.text: “The audit hook also raises on a fresh import of any module these paths name” does not say whether “these paths” means only the newly added entry points or every clock/randomness entry point listed in rule 4.
open_points.question: Which modules must cause a trap when freshly imported after removal from sys.modules: only modules named by the added list, or all modules containing any trapped entry point?
options: Trap fresh imports only of modules named by the newly added paths.
Trap fresh imports of every module containing any entry point trapped by rule 4.
open_points.default_guess: Trap every module containing any rule-4 trapped entry point.

witness.initial: A function execution starts with random already patched and present in sys.modules.
events: Agent code removes random from sys.modules.
Agent code imports random again, calls random.random(), catches any exception and returns a conforming output.
outcomes: If “these paths” covers all rule-4 paths, the fresh import is recorded as a trap and the execution is sandbox_violation.
If it covers only the newly added paths, random imports afresh and the execution can return a random value successfully.
witness.observer: The agent trying the implementation and admission see different execution outcomes.

open_points.subject: A03 stat access to /proc
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the environment holds only the runtime, code, inputs and exchange directory and mounts no other host directory, while added test 13 requires a timestamp read “on … /proc” to succeed and read zero; K-02 also says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input.”
open_points.question: Is /proc present and stat-readable by function code, or must filesystem access outside the runtime and exchange directory be refused?
options: Expose a private procfs and permit stat-family metadata reads from it, as test 13 requires.
Keep /proc absent or refuse access to it, as the isolation boundary and K-02 indicate.
open_points.default_guess: Expose a private procfs only for the stat-family behavior required by test 13.

witness.initial: An admitted function has a value output and no file input.
events: During a trial, the function calls os.stat('/proc').
It returns the resulting st_mode together with st_mtime.
outcomes: Under added test 13, stat succeeds and st_mtime is zero, so the function can also observe other /proc metadata.
Under rule 1 and K-02, /proc is unavailable or the access is a sandbox violation.
witness.observer: The agent sees either a successful trial output or a sandbox violation.

open_points.subject: A03 normalized stat results
open_points.text: “A file's timestamps read through os.stat, os.lstat, os.fstat, os.scandir and their posix namesakes are zero, whatever the file” specifies only timestamp fields and leaves every other potentially execution-specific stat field unchanged or unspecified, while A03 requires equal inputs to give equal outputs.
open_points.question: Which non-timestamp fields of stat results must be preserved, normalized, hidden or trapped so that code cannot return execution-specific filesystem identifiers?
options: Zero only timestamp fields and preserve ordinary fields such as inode, device and link count.
Normalize or hide every stat field whose value can vary between fresh sandbox executions.
Treat an attempt to expose non-deterministic stat metadata as a sandbox violation.
open_points.default_guess: Normalize sandbox-specific metadata in addition to zeroing all timestamp representations.

witness.initial: A function may create a file in its private exchange directory and has an integer output port.
events: Execution 1 creates the same scratch file and returns os.stat(path).st_ino.
Execution 2, in its required fresh environment with equal input, does the same.
outcomes: If only timestamps are changed, the two fresh files may have different inode values and therefore different output digests.
If execution-specific metadata is normalized, the two executions return the same digest as A03 requires.
witness.observer: Admission and the agent comparing trial executions see whether equal executions produce equal outputs.
